data.description:
On June 15, 2026, [URLQuery report](https://urlquery.net/report/50802d58-5095-4413-b54a-b2a7fe447ed0) preserved a custom browser program that queried Mapillary imagery near Nicosia, compared thumbnails against an embedded reference image using pixel differences, and ranked the results.

The archived screenshot shows “N 286” and 20 rows of scores, image IDs and coordinates. Network records show two Graph API HTTP 200 responses and 285 image-CDN HTTP 200 responses. These support execution and production of a ranking, not its accuracy or subsequent use. Candidate and download counts are distinct.

The contribution is this specific visual-comparison workflow and its preserved output. Transluce’s released dataset already identifies Mapillary traffic. Findings #113 and #116 establish prior art for scanner-visible output and remote computation. A September 30 check of 68 visible Findings entries found no Mapillary mention; focused web searches found no matching investigation. Neither establishes global novelty.

AI involvement is suspected from the task-specific scanner programming, the publisher’s agent-like classification, and submission metadata shared with a published agent-associated report. That metadata’s identifying value is unverified. Human-authored automation remains possible; no AI operator, provider or frontier-lab run is established.

Two related programs attempted to encode image IDs into canvas pixels, but both recorded N0; successful nonempty transfer is not demonstrated. No private-data access, credential theft, authentication bypass, compromise or malicious intent is established. This is a qualified lead about possible agent use of external computation, not a confirmed rogue-AI incident.
data.summary: Suspected agent activity: a June 15, 2026 URLQuery program compared an embedded image with Mapillary street imagery and produced 20 ranked IDs/coordinates from 286 candidates. AI involvement and provider are unverified, no compromise is established.
